facts.fact: The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics projects employment of barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists to grow 7 percent from 2025 to 2035, which it describes as much faster than the average for all occupations.
facts.quote: Overall employment of barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists is projected to grow 7 percent from 2025 to 2035, much faster than the average for all occupations.

facts.fact: The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics projects about 80,300 openings per year, on average, for barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists over the decade.
facts.quote: About 80,300 openings for barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists are projected each year, on average, over the decade.

facts.fact: The median hourly wage for barbers was $18.37 in May 2025, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.
facts.quote: The median hourly wage for barbers was $18.37 in May 2025.

facts.fact: The median hourly wage for hairdressers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists was $17.21 in May 2025, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.
facts.quote: The median hourly wage for hairdressers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists was $17.21 in May 2025.

facts.fact: All states require barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists to be licensed.
facts.quote: All states require barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists to be licensed.

facts.fact: To qualify for a license, barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists typically must graduate from a state-approved barber or cosmetology program and pass an exam.
facts.quote: To qualify for a license, candidates typically must graduate from a state-approved barber or cosmetology program and pass an exam.

facts.fact: Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists work mostly in barbershops or salons, and most are full time, although part-time work is common.
facts.quote: Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists work mostly in barbershops or salons. Most are full time, although part-time work is common.
